title: Accelerating crop breeding cycles
bottleneck: Developing a new crop variety takes 8–15 years of crossing, selection, and multi-environment trials — far slower than the pace of climate change and evolving pests. Speed breeding, genomic selection, and gene editing can compress timelines, but regulatory field-trial requirements and the biological need to test across seasons and environments impose a floor that technology hasn't broken.
why_it_blocks: Every year of breeding delay is a year farmers face new climate stresses with old genetics. The adaptation race is being lost on time alone. Every year of breeding delay is a year farmers face new climate stresses with old genetics.
current_state: Speed breeding and genomic selection cut years off in advanced programs; regulatory and testing bottlenecks still dominate timelines.
